readings.section: The Servant Songs and Zion's Restoration
readings.subsection: Prophecies of Deliverance and the Servant's Mission
readings.title: The First and the Last
readings.subtitle: A call to leave Babylon and find no peace in wickedness.
readings.text: [Isaiah 48:12] “Listen to <dn>Me</dn>, O Ya‛aqoḇ, and Yisra’ěl, <dn>My</dn> called: <dq><dn>I</dn> am <dn>He</dn>, <dn>I</dn> am the First, <dn>I</dn> am also the Last.</dq> [13] <dq>Also, <dn>My</dn> hand has laid the foundation of <dn>את</dn> the earth, and <dn>My</dn> right hand has stretched out <dn>את</dn> the heavens. <dn>I</dn> call to them, let them stand together.</dq> [14] <dq>All of you, gather yourselves, and hear! Who among them has declared <dn>את</dn> these? <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has loved him. Let him do <dn>His</dn> pleasure on Baḇel, and <dn>His</dn> arm be on the Kasdim.</dq> [15] <dq><dn>I</dn>, <dn>I</dn> have spoken, <dn>I</dn> have also called him, <dn>I</dn> have brought him, and he shall make <dn>את</dn> his way prosperous.</dq> [16] <dq>Come near to <dn>Me</dn>, hear <dn>את</dn> this: <dn>I</dn> have not spoken in secret from the beginning; from the time that it was, <dn>I</dn> was there. And now the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has sent <dn>Me</dn>, and <dn>His</dn> Spirit.”</dq> [17] Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, your Redeemer, the Set-apart One of Yisra’ěl, <dq>“<dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, teaching you what is best, leading you by the way you should go.</dq> [18] <dq>If only you had listened to <dn>My</dn> commands! Then your peace would have been like a river, and your righteousness like the waves of the sea.</dq> [19] <dq>And your seed would have been like the sand, and the offspring of your inward parts like the grains of sand. <dn>His</dn> name would not have been cut off nor destroyed from before <dn>Me</dn>.</dq> [20] <dq>Come out of Baḇel! Flee from the Kasdim! Declare <dn>את</dn> this with a voice of singing, proclaim it, send it out to the end of the earth! Say, ‘<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has redeemed <dn>את</dn> <dn>His</dn> servant Ya‛aqoḇ!’ ”</dq> [21] And they did not thirst when <dn>He</dn> led them through the deserts; <dn>He</dn> caused waters from a rock to flow for them; <dn>He</dn> split the rock, and waters gushed out. [22] <dq>“There is no peace for the wrong,”</dq> said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.”

readings.section: The Servant Songs and Zion's Restoration
readings.subsection: Prophecies of Deliverance and the Servant's Mission
readings.title: The Servant's Call
readings.subtitle: A light to the nations.
readings.text: [Isaiah 49:1] Listen to <dn>Me</dn>, O coastlands, and hear, you peoples from afar! <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has called <dn>Me</dn> from the womb, from <dn>My</dn> mother’s belly <dn>He</dn> has caused <dn>My</dn> Name to be remembered. [2] And <dn>He</dn> made <dn>My</dn> mouth like a sharp sword, in the shadow of <dn>His</dn> hand <dn>He</dn> hid <dn>Me</dn>, and made <dn>Me</dn> a polished shaft. In <dn>His</dn> quiver <dn>He</dn> hid <dn>Me</dn>.” [3] And <dn>He</dn> said to <dn>Me</dn>, <dq>‘You are <dn>My</dn> servant, O Yisra’ěl, in whom <dn>I</dn> am adorned.’</dq> [4] And <dn>I</dn> said, ‘<dn>I</dn> have laboured in vain, <dn>I</dn> have spent my strength for emptiness, and in vain. But my right-ruling is with <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and my work with my <dn>Elohim</dn>.’ ” [5] And now said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> – who formed <dn>Me</dn> from the womb to be <dn>His</dn> Servant, to bring Ya‛aqoḇ back to <dn>Him</dn>, though Yisra’ěl is not gathered to <dn>Him</dn>, yet <dn>I</dn> am esteemed in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and <dn>My</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> has been <dn>My</dn> strength – [6] and <dn>He</dn> says, <dq>“Shall it be a small matter for You to be <dn>My</dn> Servant to raise up <dn>את</dn> the tribes of Ya‛aqoḇ, and to bring back <dn>את</dn> the preserved ones of Yisra’ěl? And <dn>I</dn> shall give You as a light to the nations, to be <dn>My</dn> deliverance to the ends of the earth!”</dq> [7] Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, the Redeemer of Yisra’ěl, their Set-apart One, to the despised , to the loathed One of the nation, to the Servant of rulers, <dq>“Sovereigns shall see and arise, rulers also shall bow themselves, because of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> who is steadfast, the Set-apart One of Yisra’ěl. And <dn>He</dn> has chosen You!”</dq>

readings.section: The Servant Songs and Zion's Restoration
readings.subsection: Prophecies of Deliverance and the Servant's Mission
readings.title: Restoration in a Favorable Time
readings.subtitle: The covenant to the people.
readings.text: [Isaiah 49:8] Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“In a favourable time <dn>I</dn> shall answer You, and in the day of deliverance <dn>I</dn> shall help You – and <dn>I</dn> guard You and give You for a covenant of the people, to restore <dn>את</dn> the earth, to cause them to inherit <dn>את</dn> the ruined inheritances,</dq> [9] <dq>to say to the prisoners, ‘Go out,’ to those who are in darkness, ‘Show yourselves.’ Let them feed on the ways, and let their pasture be on all bare hills.</dq> [10] <dq>They shall not hunger nor thirst, neither heat or sun strike them, for <dn>He</dn> who has compassion on them shall lead them, even by fountains of water guide them.</dq> [11] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> shall make all <dn>My</dn> mountains a way, and <dn>My</dn> highways raised up.</dq> [12] <dq>See, these come from far away, and see, those from the north and the west, and these from the land of Sinim.”</dq> [13] Sing, O heavens, rejoice, O earth! And break out in singing, O mountains! For <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall comfort <dn>His</dn> people and have compassion on <dn>His</dn> afflicted ones.

readings.section: The Servant Songs and Zion's Restoration
readings.subsection: Prophecies of Deliverance and the Servant's Mission
readings.title: Zion Not Forgotten
readings.subtitle: God's enduring love and promise of deliverance.
readings.text: [Isaiah 49:14] But Tsiyon says, “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has forsaken me, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has forgotten me.” [15] <dq>“Would a woman forget her nursing child, and not have compassion on the son of her womb? Though they forget, <dn>I</dn> never forget you.</dq> [16] <dq>See, <dn>I</dn> have inscribed you on the palms of <dn>My</dn> hands; your walls are always before <dn>Me</dn>.</dq> [17] <dq>Your sons shall hurry, your destroyers and those who laid you waste depart from you.</dq> [18] <dq>Lift up your eyes round about and see, all of them gather together and come to you. As <dn>I</dn> live,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“you shall put on all of them as an ornament, and bind them on you as a bride does.</dq> [19] <dq>For your wastes, and your deserted places, and the land of your destruction, shall soon be too narrow for the inhabitants, while those who swallowed you up are far away.</dq> [20] <dq>The sons of your bereavement shall yet say in your ears, ‘The place is too narrow for me, make room for me to live.’</dq> [21] <dq>And you shall say in your heart, ‘Who has brought forth these for me, since <dn>I</dn> am bereaved and barren, an exile, and wandering to and fro? And who reared them? See, <dn>I</dn> was left alone – from where did these come?’ ”</dq> [22] Thus said the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“See, <dn>I</dn> lift <dn>My</dn> hand up to the nations, and set up <dn>My</dn> banner for the peoples; and they shall bring your sons in their arms, and your daughters carried on their shoulders;</dq> [23] <dq>And sovereigns shall be your foster fathers, and their sovereignesses your nursing mothers. They bow down to you with their faces to the earth, and lick up <dn>את</dn> the dust of your feet. And you shall know that <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> – those who wait for <dn>Me</dn> shall not be ashamed.”</dq> [24] Is prey taken from the mighty, and the captives of the righteous delivered? [25] Yet thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“Even the captives of the mighty are taken away, and the prey of the ruthless is delivered; and <dn>I</dn> strive with him who strives with you, and <dn>I</dn> save <dn>את</dn> your children.</dq> [26] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> shall feed those who oppress you with their own flesh, and let them drink their own blood as sweet wine. All flesh shall know that <dn>I</dn>, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, am your Saviour, and your Redeemer, the Mighty One of Ya‛aqoḇ.”</dq>

readings.section: The Servant Songs and Zion's Restoration
readings.subsection: Prophecies of Deliverance and the Servant's Mission
readings.title: Israel's Transgressions
readings.subtitle: Sold for crookedness, not for God's lack of power.
readings.text: [Isaiah 50:1] Thus says <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“Where is the certificate of your mother’s divorce, whom <dn>I</dn> have put away? Or which of <dn>My</dn> creditors is it to whom <dn>I</dn> have sold you? Look, you were sold for your crookednesses, and your mother was put away for your transgressions.</dq> [2] <dq>When <dn>I</dn> came, why was there no man? When <dn>I</dn> called, why was there no one to answer? Was <dn>My</dn> hand too short to ransom? Or have <dn>I</dn> no power to deliver? See, by <dn>My</dn> rebuke <dn>I</dn> dry up the sea, <dn>I</dn> make the rivers a wilderness; their fish stink for there is not water, and die of thirst.</dq> [3] <dq><dn>I</dn> clothe <dn>את</dn> the heavens with darkness, and <dn>I</dn> make sackcloth their covering.”</dq>

readings.section: The Servant Songs and Zion's Restoration
readings.subsection: Prophecies of Deliverance and the Servant's Mission
readings.title: The Obedient Servant
readings.subtitle: His suffering and vindication.
readings.text: [Isaiah 50:4] The Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has given <dn>Me</dn> the tongue of taught ones, that <dn>I</dn> should know to help the weary with a word. <dn>He</dn> wakes <dn>Me</dn> morning by morning, he wakes <dn>My</dn> ear to hear as taught ones. [5] The Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has opened <dn>My</dn> ear, and <dn>I</dn> was not rebellious, nor did <dn>I</dn> turn away. [6] <dn>I</dn> gave <dn>My</dn> back to those who struck <dn>Me</dn>, and <dn>My</dn> cheeks to those who plucked out the beard, <dn>I</dn> did not hide <dn>My</dn> face from humiliation and spitting. [7] And the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> helps <dn>Me</dn>, therefore <dn>I</dn> shall not be humiliated. So <dn>I</dn> have set <dn>My</dn> face like a flint, and <dn>I</dn> know that <dn>I</dn> am not put to shame. [8] Near is <dn>He</dn> who declares <dn>Me</dn> right. Who would contend with <dn>Me</dn>? Let us stand together. Who is <dn>My</dn> adversary? Let him come near <dn>Me</dn>. [9] See, the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> helps <dn>Me</dn>. Who would declare <dn>Me</dn> wrong? See, all of them wear out like a garment, a moth eats them. [10] Who among you is fearing <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, obeying the voice of <dn>His</dn> Servant, that has walked in darkness and has no light? Let him trust in the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and lean upon his <dn>Elohim</dn>! [11] See, all you who light a fire, girding on burning arrows: walk in the light of your fire and in the burning arrows you have lit. From <dn>My</dn> hand you shall have this: you shall lie down in grief!

readings.section: The Servant Songs and Zion's Restoration
readings.subsection: Prophecies of Deliverance and the Servant's Mission
readings.title: Look to the Rock
readings.subtitle: A call to trust in God's everlasting righteousness.
readings.text: [Isaiah 51:1] <dq>“Listen to <dn>Me</dn>, you who pursue righteousness, seeking <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>: Look to the rock you were hewn from, and to the hole of the pit you were dug from.</dq> [2] <dq>Look to Aḇraham your father, and to Sarah who bore you. For he was alone when <dn>I</dn> called him, and <dn>I</dn> blessed him and increased him.</dq> [3] <dq>For <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall comfort Tsiyon, <dn>He</dn> shall comfort all her waste places. For <dn>He</dn> makes her wilderness like Ěḏen, and her desert like the garden of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. Joy and gladness are found in it, thanksgiving and the voice of song.</dq> [4] <dq>Listen to <dn>Me</dn>, <dn>My</dn> people, and give ear to <dn>Me</dn>, O <dn>My</dn> nation, for the Torah goes forth from <dn>Me</dn>, and <dn>My</dn> right-ruling <dn>I</dn> set as a light to peoples.</dq> [5] <dq><dn>My</dn> righteousness is near, <dn>My</dn> deliverance shall go forth, and <dn>My</dn> arms judge peoples. Coastlands wait upon <dn>Me</dn>, and for <dn>My</dn> arm they wait expectantly.</dq> [6] <dq>Lift up your eyes to the heavens, and look on the earth beneath, for the heavens shall vanish like smoke, and the earth wear out like a garment, and those who dwell in it die as gnats. But <dn>My</dn> deliverance is forever, and <dn>My</dn> righteousness is not broken.</dq> [7] <dq>Listen to <dn>Me</dn>, you who know righteousness, a people in whose heart is <dn>My</dn> Torah: do not fear <dn>את</dn> the reproach of men, nor be afraid of their revilings.</dq> [8] <dq>For a moth eats them like a garment, and a worm eats them like wool; but <dn>My</dn> righteousness is forever, and <dn>My</dn> deliverance to all generations.”</dq>

readings.section: The Servant Songs and Zion's Restoration
readings.subsection: Prophecies of Deliverance and the Servant's Mission
readings.title: Awake, O Arm of YeHoVaH
readings.subtitle: A plea for deliverance and God's comforting response.
readings.text: [Isaiah 51:9] Awake, awake, put on strength, O arm of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>! Awake as in days of old, everlasting generations. Was it not You who cut Rahaḇ apart, and pierced the Crocodile? [10] Was it not You who dried up the sea, the waters of the great deep, who made the depths of the sea a way for the redeemed to pass over? [11] And let the ransomed of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> return. And they shall come to Tsiyon with singing, with everlasting joy on their heads. Let them attain joy and gladness; sorrow and sighing shall flee away. [12] <dq>“<dn>I</dn>, <dn>I</dn> am <dn>He</dn> who comforts you. Who are you that you should be afraid of man that dies, and of the son of man who is made like grass?</dq> [13] <dq>And you have forgotten <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your Maker who stretched out the heavens and laid the foundations of the earth, and you continually fear, all the day, because of the rage of the oppressor, as he has prepared to destroy. And where is the rage of the oppressor?</dq> [14] <dq>Bowed, he hastens to be loosened, that he should not die in the pit, and that his bread should not fail.</dq> [15] <dq>But <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, stirring up the sea, and its waves roar. <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts is <dn>His</dn> Name.</dq> [16] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> have put <dn>My</dn> Words in your mouth, and with the shadow of <dn>My</dn> hand <dn>I</dn> have covered you, to plant the heavens and lay the foundations of the earth, and to say to Tsiyon, ‘You are <dn>My</dn> people.’ ”</dq>

readings.section: The Servant Songs and Zion's Restoration
readings.subsection: Prophecies of Deliverance and the Servant's Mission
readings.title: The Cup of Wrath
readings.subtitle: Jerusalem's suffering will be transferred to her oppressors.
readings.text: [Isaiah 51:17] Awake, awake yourself! Rise up, O Yerushalayim, you who have drunk at the hand of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>את</dn> the cup of <dn>His</dn> wrath. You have drunk <dn>את</dn> the dregs of the cup of reeling, and drained it out. [18] Of all the sons she bore, she has none to guide her. And of all the sons she has brought up, none is strengthening her hand. [19] Both these are coming upon you – who is sorry for you?: Ruin and destruction, scarcity of food and sword. How shall <dn>I</dn> comfort you? [20] Your sons have fainted, they lie at the head of all the streets, like a gazelle in a net. They are filled with the wrath of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, the rebuke of your <dn>Elohim</dn>. [21] Therefore please hear this, you afflicted and drunk, but not with wine. [22] Thus said your Master, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and your <dn>Elohim</dn>, who pleads the cause of <dn>His</dn> people, <dq>“See, <dn>I</dn> shall take out of your hand <dn>את</dn> the cup of reeling, <dn>את</dn> the dregs of the cup of <dn>My</dn> wrath – never again shall you drink it.</dq> [23] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> shall put it into the hand of those who afflict you, who have said to your being, ‘Bow down, and we pass over you.’ And you made your back like the ground, and as the street, to walk over.”</dq>

readings.section: The Servant Songs and Zion's Restoration
readings.subsection: Prophecies of Deliverance and the Servant's Mission
readings.title: Awake, O Zion
readings.subtitle: Put on your strength and garments of splendour.
readings.text: [Isaiah 52:1] Awake, awake! Put on your strength, O Tsiyon, put on your garments of splendour, O Yerushalayim, the set-apart city! For no more do the uncircumcised and the unclean come into you. [2] Shake yourself from the dust, arise, and sit down, O Yerushalayim. Loose yourself from the bonds of your neck, O captive daughter of Tsiyon! [3] For thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“You have been sold for naught, and you are redeemed not with silver.”</dq> [4] For thus said the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“At first <dn>My</dn> people went down into Mitsrayim to sojourn there, and Ashshur oppressed them without cause.</dq> [5] <dq>And now, what have <dn>I</dn> here,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“that <dn>My</dn> people are taken away for naught? Those who rule over them make them wail,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“and <dn>My</dn> Name is despised all day continually.</dq> [6] <dq>Therefore <dn>My</dn> people shall know <dn>My</dn> Name, in that day, for <dn>I</dn> am the One who is speaking. See, it is <dn>I</dn>.”</dq>

readings.section: The Servant Songs and Zion's Restoration
readings.subsection: Prophecies of Deliverance and the Servant's Mission
readings.title: The Good News of Deliverance
readings.subtitle: The feet of him who brings good news.
readings.text: [Isaiah 52:7] How pleasant upon the mountains are the feet of him who brings good news, who proclaims peace, who brings good news, who proclaims deliverance, who says to Tsiyon, “Your <dn>Elohim</dn> reigns!” [8] The voice of your watchmen! They shall lift up their voices, together they shout for joy, because eye to eye they see the return of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> to Tsiyon. [9] Break forth into joy, sing together, you waste places of Yerushalayim! For <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall comfort <dn>His</dn> people, <dn>He</dn> shall redeem Yerushalayim. [10] <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall lay bare <dn>את</dn> <dn>His</dn> set-apart arm in the eyes of all the nations. And all the ends of the earth shall see <dn>את</dn> the deliverance of our <dn>Elohim</dn>. [11] Turn aside! Turn aside! Come out from there, touch not the unclean. Come out of her midst, be clean, you who bear the vessels of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [12] For you shall not come out in haste, nor go in flight. For <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is going before you, and the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl is your rear guard.
